subject: Running GGIR part 4 on 24 hour data

messages.author: acbe60780cfdd53f
messages.subject: Running GGIR part 4 on 24 hour data
parts:
Hello, 

My colleague and I are currently working as research assistants at the Vascular Function Lab at Smith College. We are currently investigating menopausal hot flashes as they relate to sleep disruptions and physical activity levels. 

For our study, we had participants wear an accelerometer for 24 hours. We are interested in looking at variables that are in the Part 4 Sleep Summary (WASO, number of awakenings, etc.) but got an error message after running the code pasted below:

sleep_algorithm <- "vanHees2015"
GGIR::GGIR(datadir = "ourdatadir", 
outputdir="outputdir",
minimum_MM_length.part5 = 21.6,
dofirstpage = FALSE,
do.parallel = FALSE,
strategy = 1,
includedaycrit = 21.6,
excludefirstlast.part5 = FALSE,
do.enmo = TRUE,
acc.metric = "ENMO",
threshold.lig = c(44.8),
threshold.mod = c(100.6),
threshold.vig = c(428.8),
HASIB.algo = sleep_algorithm)

Generate visual reports

[1] "File 006_V1 (2021-06-15).gt3x"

Error in `[.data.frame`(daysummary_tmp, , MainMetric) :

  object 'MainMetric' not found


We are able to obtain what we need from Part 4 but am unsure if this error in Part 5 may affect the Part 4 data. If we are only looking at the Part 4 data right now, would this error impact the output? Could we use the 24-hour data to only analyze sleep without looking at physical activity during the day?


Thank you very much and we look forward to hearing from you.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Running GGIR part 4 on 24 hour data
parts:
Generate visual reports

[1] "File 006_V1 (2021-06-15).gt3x"

Error in `[.data.frame`(daysummary_tmp, , MainMetric) :

  object 'MainMetric' not found

This only affects the visual report and not the part 4 and 5 output.

To address the issue it would be good to understand:
  • What version of GGIR are you using?
  • Did you already create the part2_daysummary.csv file?
  • If not, make sure you run GGIR at least once with do.report = 2
  • If yes, is there a column mean_ENMO_mg_.... in your part 2 daysummary file?

Best, Vincent


Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
